primary.title: The Gospels
primary.author: Matthew, Mark, Luke, John
primary.rationale: The Gospels are the primary accounts of Jesus' life and teachings, considered by Christians to be divinely inspired. While authorship is debated, they are directly attributed to the apostles or their close associates.

primary.title: The Acts of the Apostles
primary.author: Luke
primary.rationale: Acts, traditionally attributed to Luke, provides an account of the early Christian church and the spread of Jesus' message after his ascension. It offers insights into the immediate impact of his teachings.

primary.title: The Epistles of Paul
primary.author: Paul the Apostle
primary.rationale: While not direct accounts of Jesus' life, Paul's letters are the earliest surviving Christian writings. They offer theological interpretations of Jesus' life, death, and resurrection, and provide context for early Christian beliefs.

secondary.title: Jesus: A Revolutionary Biography
secondary.author: John Dominic Crossan
secondary.rationale: Crossan offers a scholarly reconstruction of Jesus' life, placing him within his historical and social context as a Galilean peasant and social critic.

secondary.title: The Historical Jesus: The Life of a Mediterranean Jewish Peasant
secondary.author: John P. Meier
secondary.rationale: Meier's multi-volume work is a comprehensive and critical examination of the evidence for the historical Jesus, employing rigorous historical-critical methods.

secondary.title: Jesus and the Victory of Judaism
secondary.author: Richard A. Horsley
secondary.rationale: Horsley analyzes Jesus within the context of Jewish peasant society and its resistance to Roman occupation, arguing for Jesus as a leader of social and religious change.

suggestions.notes: Primary sources for Jesus are exclusively religious texts, primarily the New Testament Gospels and Epistles. Historical consensus on their direct authorship and precise dating varies. Secondary sources represent major scholarly attempts to reconstruct the historical Jesus from these texts and other contemporary evidence.
